info.title: Paer User API
info.description:
> ## 👋 Three APIs, one site
>
> This documentation site bundles **three Paer APIs** under a single nav.
> Right now you're looking at the **User API**. To see the others
> (**Quotes API**, **Beneficiary API**), look for the **dropdown at the
> top of the left sidebar** — just above the search box. It currently
> reads **"User API ▾"**. Click it to switch.

The **User API** is the source-of-truth for *who you are* on the Paer
platform. Every other service (`api.paer.dk`, `beneficiary-api.paer.dk`)
authenticates by introspecting the keys you mint here.

> **New here?** Browse the **Quotes API** first (use the sidebar
> dropdown) — that's where actual money moves. This service is the
> identity + KYB plumbing that lets you call it.

## What lives here

- **Companies + KYB lifecycle**: every customer is a company. Onboarding
  goes `not_started → in_review → verified | rejected` via append-only
  KYB decisions. Risk tier `low | medium | high` drives re-verification
  cadence.
- **Users**: power-of-attorney holders inside a company. Each user has a
  role — **A** (full write), **B** (write requires a 2nd A/B signature
  for KYB-grade decisions), **C** (read-only). A company always has ≥1
  active A-user.
- **API keys**: `paer_sk_...` — minted by users, scoped to their company,
  presented as `X-API-Key` to every other service.
- **Web auth**: signup, email verification, password reset, mandatory
  MFA (TOTP + WebAuthn passkeys), backup codes, sessions. Used by
  `app.paer.dk`.

## Getting started — full new-customer flow

```
POST /v1/auth/signup                    ← create company shell + first user
GET  ...verify email link...            ← link arrives via SES
POST /v1/auth/login                     ← returns MFA challenge token
POST /v1/auth/mfa/totp/enroll/start     ← QR code for authenticator app
POST /v1/auth/mfa/totp/enroll/confirm   ← + first 6-digit code
POST /v1/auth/login/mfa                 ← totp code, returns session token
POST /v1/api-keys                       ← mint your first paer_sk_... key
```

A Paer-Internal operator approves your KYB decision (we'll be in touch
during the pilot — Q4 2026 launch onwards this becomes a self-serve
KYB-provider integration).

## How introspection works (for service authors)

If you're building a Paer-Internal service that also wants to accept
customer keys, call:

```
POST /v1/keys/introspect
  Headers:
    X-Service-Auth: <hex hmac-sha256(body, SERVICE_HMAC_SECRET)>
    Content-Type:  application/json
  Body:
    {"key": "paer_sk_..."}
  Response:
    {"active": true, "key_id": "...", "user_id": "...",
     "company_id": "...", "role": "A", "company_kyb_status": "verified", ...}
```

Cache positive results 30 s, negative 5 s, fail closed on transport
errors. The reference client lives in
`paer-aps/paer-quotes-api/app/clients/user_api.py` and
`paer-aps/paer-beneficiary-api/app/clients/user_api.py`.

## Conventions

- Datetimes UTC ISO 8601. Currency ISO 4217. Country ISO 3166 alpha-2.
- Audit log carries `user_id`, `company_id`, `client_ip`, `user_agent`,
  `request_id` — 6+ year retention per AML 2024/1624.

get.description: Liveness + DB readiness. Fails closed on any DB error.

post.description:
Step 2 for users with already-enrolled MFA. Verifies one of the
provided proofs and exchanges the challenge for a session cookie.

Create a pending TOTP factor + return QR. Caller follows up with /enroll
once the user has scanned the QR and submitted the first code.

Validate the first TOTP code → confirm factor → if first MFA factor,
generate backup codes + return them ONCE → issue session cookie.

Returns WebAuthn PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions for the browser's
navigator.credentials.create() call. The returned `challenge_token`
must be passed back in /enroll along with the credential.

body.challenge_token MUST be a WebAuthn challenge from /passkey/init.
Verifies the credential, persists the factor, issues session cookie.

Returns WebAuthn AuthenticationOptions for an existing-passkey login.
After the browser signs the assertion, POST it to /v1/auth/login/mfa
with passkey_response + passkey_challenge_token=this challenge.

schema.title: Response List Factors V1 Auth Mfa Factors Get

post.description:
Returns a fresh batch of 10 backup codes, supersedes the previous batch.
Returned ONCE — caller must surface them immediately.

schema.title: Response Regenerate Backup Codes V1 Auth Mfa Backup Codes Regenerate Post

post.description:
Resolve a session token → user info or `valid=false`. 200 in both
cases so callers can briefly cache negatives. Touches the session
(slides expiry) on success, mirroring the cookie path.

Revoke a session by plaintext token. Idempotent — unknown / already
revoked tokens still return `revoked=true` so paer-app's logout button
is a one-click no-replay action.

schema.title: Response List Users V1 Users Get
Response List Own Keys V1 Api Keys Get

post.description:
Mint a new key for the calling user. Role inherits from the user (A/B/C).

Note: a C-user calling this gets 403 from the service layer. They can
authenticate (since they hold a C-key) but can't bootstrap a higher tier.

Customer signals 'KYB profile filled in, please review'. Flips
kyb_status to in_review AND drops a `customer_submitted` row into the
KybDecision queue so operators see it on the dashboard. Operators
close the loop with a fresh verified/rejected decision via
/v1/admin/companies/{id}/kyb-decisions; that auto-withdraws the
customer-submitted row.

put.description:
Local-env-only upload sink. Customer's PUT request body is the file bytes.
The presign endpoint hands out URLs pointing here; in non-local env the URL
points at S3 and this route is unreachable.

get.description:
Local-env-only download sink. The presigned-GET URL handed out by
storage.presign_download in local mode points here.

ApiKeyCreate.title: ApiKeyCreate
ApiKeyCreate.description: End-user mints a key for themselves. Role is inherited from the user.

ApiKeyCreated.title: ApiKeyCreated
ApiKeyCreated.description: Returned ONCE on creation. Contains the plaintext key — never re-sendable.

ApiKeyInfo.title: ApiKeyInfo
ApiKeyInfo.description: Public representation — never includes the plaintext.

expected_corridors.title: Expected Corridors
expected_corridors.description: ISO-2 destination country codes the customer expects to send to.

IntrospectRequest.title: IntrospectRequest
IntrospectRequest.description: Body for `POST /v1/keys/introspect` — called by paer-quotes-api / paer-beneficiary-api.

IntrospectResponse.title: IntrospectResponse
IntrospectResponse.description: Metadata bundle returned to the calling service. Cached for 30s on their side.

KybDocumentPresignRequest.title: KybDocumentPresignRequest
KybDocumentPresignRequest.description:
Body for `POST /v1/companies/me/kyb-documents/presign-upload`.

Customer declares what they're about to upload; we return a short-lived
upload URL. The customer then PUTs the file to that URL and calls back
via `POST /v1/companies/me/kyb-documents` with the same `storage_key`.

KybDocumentPresignResponse.title: KybDocumentPresignResponse
KybDocumentPresignResponse.description:
The customer must PUT to `upload_url` with `Content-Type: <content_type>`
within `expires_in` seconds, then call back with `storage_key` to record.

LoginChallengeResponse.title: LoginChallengeResponse
LoginChallengeResponse.description:
Returned when login step 1 succeeds (password OK + email verified).

`requires_enrollment=True` means the user has zero confirmed MFA factors;
the next call should be /v1/auth/mfa/totp/init or /v1/auth/mfa/passkey/init
using this challenge. Once a factor is enrolled, the same challenge can
be exchanged for a session.

`requires_enrollment=False` + non-empty `available_factors` means existing
user with MFA — call /v1/auth/login/mfa with a proof of one factor.

company_id.title: Company Id
company_id.description: Optional. Required only when the email exists in multiple companies; otherwise the unique match is used. Most pilot users will leave this blank — they're in exactly one company.

passkey_challenge_token.title: Passkey Challenge Token
passkey_challenge_token.description: The challenge token returned from /v1/auth/mfa/passkey/init. Required when passkey_response is provided.

MfaLoginRequest.title: MfaLoginRequest
MfaLoginRequest.description: Body for POST /v1/auth/login/mfa. Provide exactly ONE of the three proofs.

MfaSessionResponse.title: MfaSessionResponse
MfaSessionResponse.description:
Returned when login OR enrollment completes successfully. Contains user
info + (on first enrollment) the one-shot backup codes the user MUST save.

Also carries the plaintext session token so server-side callers (paer-app)
can set their own cookie on the right domain (app.paer.dk) without parsing
Set-Cookie. Browsers calling user-api directly can ignore these fields and
rely on the Set-Cookie header instead.

PasskeyInitResponse.title: PasskeyInitResponse
PasskeyInitResponse.description:
The `options` blob is the WebAuthn PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions
(or RequestOptions for authentication) — pass it directly to the
browser's navigator.credentials.create / get APIs.

SessionValidateResponse.title: SessionValidateResponse
SessionValidateResponse.description:
200 in both valid + invalid cases (so callers can cache negatives briefly
without conflating with service-down). 401 reserved for HMAC failures.

signing_authority.title: Signing Authority
signing_authority.description: Solo, Joint-2, Joint-all, etc. Free text for now.

Signatory.title: Signatory
Signatory.description: Authorised signatory — power-of-attorney holder per the company's articles.

SignupRequest.title: SignupRequest
SignupRequest.description: Body for POST /v1/signup — atomic create-company + create-user + send-verification.

message.title: Message
message.default: Signup received. Check your email to verify the address.

SignupResponse.title: SignupResponse
SignupResponse.description:
We deliberately do NOT include the verification token in the response
— it goes only to the email. Returning a generic ack prevents probing
whether an email exists in the system.

UBO.title: UBO
UBO.description:
Ultimate beneficial owner.

Required by AML Regulation 2024/1624 and PSD3. Threshold for inclusion is
25% ownership or effective control (paer-brain V6). Screening status is
populated post-IDV by the configured KYB provider.

ServiceAuth.description: HMAC-SHA256 of the request body, signed with SERVICE_HMAC_SECRET.
ServiceAuth.name: X-Service-Auth

ApiKey.description: End-user or operator API key. Format: `paer_sk_<43>`.
ApiKey.name: X-API-Key

SessionToken.description: Plaintext user-api session token — used by paer-app to act as a logged-in user. MUST be accompanied by `X-Service-Auth: hmac_sha256(SERVICE_HMAC_SECRET, session_token)`. TLS provides request integrity; the HMAC proves the caller possesses the inter-service secret.
SessionToken.name: X-Session-Token
